items.text: You do not have to pick coding or PCM this week.
A coding certificate never replaces the stream at the seat entry requirement.
Other stream questions are answered in the Stream Selection guides.

blocks.heading: Branches Use Coding, and Do You Need

items.text: Most branches use some code, but the amount differs a lot.
You do not need coding before B.Tech computer science, because most first-year programming courses start from the basics.
Plan by stage and outcome, not by hours counted.
Make a few small programs that solve a real chore, such as a marks calculator or a quiz.
Use what you built to judge whether you like building.
Routes are rated Scalable, Scalable with a business layer, or Not so scalable, by how far your own effort can grow beyond a salary.
First, because it is the only route that keeps the seat safe and also starts your proof years before most of your batch.
Who pays you Later, internship teams and employers, and small clients who need a simple tool.
Work through the Four questions to answer before you commit to test the choice, then pass the Three proofs to pass before you earn to show it is working.
Try one chapter set from Class 11 maths and one small program, then notice which one you return to without being told.
Count board preparation, tuition, sleep and the fee.

blocks.heading: Proof for an Employer Marks and Rank
rows: Maths and physics courses assume you already know the Class 12 base.
A first programming course feels easier if you have already written some code.
Marks and rank. They help at the college entry requirement and fade quickly after.
Finished projects you can explain. These count at internship time.
Shows whether you like maths and physics reasoning, which core branches use heavily.
Shows whether you like debugging and building, which computer science branches use heavily.
Gaps in Class 11 maths are hard to fill later, because each chapter leans on the last.
Starting in college is common and still works, but you will have fewer finished projects to show.
A strong base helps you frame problems and check results.
Routine code is getting cheaper, so judging code matters more than typing it.
